Layout newshape objects

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_layout_newshape.Rd

Properties of layout.newshape.

Usage

go_layout_newshape(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  drawdirection = NULL,
  fillcolor = NULL,
  fillrule = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  layer = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  legendgroup = NULL,
  legendgrouptitle = NULL,
  legendrank = NULL,
  legendwidth = NULL,
  line = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  showlegend = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_newshape_label(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  font = NULL,
  padding = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  textangle = NULL,
  textposition = NULL,
  texttemplate = NULL,
  texttemplatefallback = NULL,
  xanchor = NULL,
  yanchor = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_newshape_label_font(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  lineposition = NULL,
  shadow = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  textcase = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  font = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle_font(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  lineposition = NULL,
  shadow = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  textcase = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_newshape_line(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  dash = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from (constructors). Named arguments take precedence.

...

Further properties, including nested properties in "magic underscore" form, e.g. marker_size = 10 for marker = list(size = 10). Property values may be one-sided formulas, evaluated in data for add_*() functions.

drawdirection

When `dragmode` is set to "drawrect", "drawline" or "drawcircle" this limits the drag to be horizontal, vertical or diagonal. Using "diagonal" there is no limit e.g. in drawing lines in any direction. "ortho" limits the draw to be either horizontal or vertical. "horizontal" allows horizontal extend. "vertical" allows vertical extend. One of "ortho", "horizontal", "vertical", "diagonal".

fillcolor

Sets the color filling new shapes' interior. Please note that if using a fillcolor with alpha greater than half, drag inside the active shape starts moving the shape underneath, otherwise a new shape could be started over. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

fillrule

Determines the path's interior. For more info please visit https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Attribute/fill-rule One of "evenodd", "nonzero".

label

Named list or go_layout_newshape_label() object.

layer

Specifies whether new shapes are drawn below gridlines ("below"), between gridlines and traces ("between") or above traces ("above"). One of "below", "above", "between".

legend

Sets the reference to a legend to show new shape in. References to these legends are "legend", "legend2", "legend3", etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc. Subplot id: "legend", "legend2", "legend3", ....

legendgroup

Sets the legend group for new shape. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items. String.

legendgrouptitle

Named list or go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle() object.

legendrank

Sets the legend rank for new shape. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with "reversed" `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. Number.

legendwidth

Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for new shape. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

line

Named list or go_layout_newshape_line() object.

name

Sets new shape name. The name appears as the legend item. String.

opacity

Sets the opacity of new shapes. Number in the interval [0, 1].

showlegend

Determines whether or not new shape is shown in the legend. Logical.

visible

Determines whether or not new shape is visible. If "legendonly", the shape is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible). One of "legendonly", TRUE, FALSE.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

font

go_layout_newshape_label(): Sets the new shape label text font. Named list or go_layout_newshape_label_font() object.

go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle(): Sets this legend group's title font. Named list or go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle_font() object.

padding

Sets padding (in px) between edge of label and edge of new shape. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

text

go_layout_newshape_label(): Sets the text to display with the new shape. It is also used for legend item if `name` is not provided. String.

go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle(): Sets the title of the legend group. String.

textangle

Sets the angle at which the label text is drawn with respect to the horizontal. For lines, angle "auto" is the same angle as the line. For all other shapes, angle "auto" is horizontal. Angle in degrees.

textposition

Sets the position of the label text relative to the new shape. Supported values for rectangles, circles and paths are "top left", "top center", "top right", "middle left", "middle center", "middle right", "bottom left", "bottom center", and "bottom right". Supported values for lines are "start", "middle", and "end". Default: "middle center" for rectangles, circles, and paths; "middle" for lines. One of "top left", "top center", "top right", "middle left", "middle center", "middle right", "bottom left", "bottom center", "bottom right", "start", "middle", "end".

texttemplate

Template string used for rendering the new shape's label. Note that this will override `text`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "x0: %{x0}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{x0:$.2f}". See https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{x0|%m %b %Y}". See https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. A single multiplication or division operation may be applied to numeric variables, and combined with d3 number formatting, for example "Length in cm: %{x0"2.54}", "%{slope"60:.1f} meters per second." For log axes, variable values are given in log units. For date axes, x/y coordinate variables and center variables use datetimes, while all other variable values use values in ms. Finally, the template string has access to variables `x0`, `x1`, `y0`, `y1`, `slope`, `dx`, `dy`, `width`, `height`, `length`, `xcenter`, `ycenter`, `simpleXVariables` and `simpleYVariables`. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. String.

texttemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

xanchor

Sets the label's horizontal position anchor This anchor binds the specified `textposition` to the "left", "center" or "right" of the label text. For example, if `textposition` is set to "top right" and `xanchor` to "right" then the right-most portion of the label text lines up with the right-most edge of the new shape. One of "auto", "left", "center", "right".

yanchor

Sets the label's vertical position anchor This anchor binds the specified `textposition` to the "top", "middle" or "bottom" of the label text. For example, if `textposition` is set to "top right" and `yanchor` to "top" then the top-most portion of the label text lines up with the top-most edge of the new shape. One of "top", "middle", "bottom".

color

go_layout_newshape_label_font(), go_layout_newshape_legendgrouptitle_font(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_layout_newshape_line(): Sets the line color. By default uses either dark grey or white to increase contrast with background color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

family

HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String.

lineposition

Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none".

shadow

Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String.

size

Number in the interval [1, Inf].

style

Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic".

textcase

Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower".

variant

Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase".

weight

Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000].

dash

Sets the dash style of lines. Set to a dash type string ("solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", or "longdashdot") or a dash length list in px (eg "5px,10px,2px,2px"). One of "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot", or a string matching "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?((,|\\s)\\s*\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?)*$".

width

Sets the line width (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

Value

Each go_*() function returns a graph object of the same class as its name; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_layout_newshape() and the nested object constructors below create validated graph objects (named lists). Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when an object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify()).
